title: Step-ups Using Stairs: Leg Workout at Home Without Equipment
intro: Step-ups are an exercise where you step up and down one stair, great for strengthening your legs and raising your heart rate. All you need is the stairs at home or one sturdy step.
muscles: Front thighs (quadriceps), glutes, back thighs (hamstrings) and calves. It also trains balance and heart stamina.
steps: Stand facing the bottom step. Hold the stair railing if needed.
Place your whole right foot on the step.
Press through your right heel and step up until you're standing upright.
Step down slowly, right foot first.
Repeat for the set number of reps, then switch to your left leg.
mistakes: Only your toes on the step. This leaves your heel hanging and puts more pressure on your knee.
Knee caving inward while stepping up. Make sure your knee lines up with your toes.
Bouncing off the bottom foot. Let the foot on the step do the work.
easier: Use the lowest step, hold the wall or stair railing, and go slowly.
harder: Hold a bag with a few books or two water bottles, or lift the knee of your other leg to hip height when you reach the top.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 sets, 8-10 reps on each leg, rest 45-60 seconds between sets. Do it 2-3 times a week.
safety: Make sure the floor and stairs aren't slippery, and wear stable shoes or go barefoot with a steady footing. Stop if you feel sharp knee pain, dizziness or chest pain, and see a doctor or physio if the pain persists.

faq.q: I live in a condo with no stairs inside. Can I still do this?
faq.a: Yes, you can use the building's emergency staircase, or a low, sturdy bench that doesn't move. Don't use plastic chairs or chairs with wheels.

faq.q: My knees make sounds when I do step-ups. Is that normal?
faq.a: Sounds without pain are usually nothing to worry about. But if the sound comes with pain or swelling, stop and get a doctor's or physio's opinion.

faq.q: Can step-ups slim down my thighs?
faq.a: Step-ups strengthen your thigh muscles, but fat can't be removed from just one spot. Fat comes down overall when your eating and daily movement are consistent.
